hypothesis: Theorem AG-1 (paper papers/alignment_as_ensemble_governance/paper.md) predicts that on a 4-state Markov world with viable region V={0,1,2}, unviable state {3}, uniform random policy over actions {stay, move}, and per-step leakage rate beta=0.05 by construction, the survival probability Pr[q(X_t) in V for all t <= T] is at least (1-beta)^T at every T in {1, 3, 5, 10, 20}, computed exactly by matrix powers. On this world the bound is tight (equality) at every T because every row of the V-sub-kernel sums to exactly 1-beta. Theorem AG-2 predicts extending V to V'=Z gives survival 1.0 at every T (trivially, since beta_Z=0).

gates.AGP_AG1_LOWER_BOUND_HOLDS_AT_EVERY_T: For every T in {1, 3, 5, 10, 20}, the exact survival probability under the coarse Markov kernel restricted to V is at least (1 - beta)^T, within 1e-12 numerical tolerance.
gates.AGP_AG1_LOWER_BOUND_TIGHTNESS: At T=1, exact survival probability equals (1 - beta) = 0.95 exactly (within 1e-12).
gates.AGP_AG2_VIABILITY_INHERITED_BY_SUPERSET: When V is extended to V'=Z (everything viable), exact survival is 1.0 at every T (within 1e-12).
gates.AGP_AG_SURVIVAL_MONOTONE_DECREASING_IN_T: Exact survival probability on V is weakly monotone non-increasing across the horizon sweep {1, 3, 5, 10, 20}.

world.policy: uniform random over actions at every viable state

compute.sampling: exact enumeration of the 4x4 coarse Markov kernel and its matrix powers up to T=20; no Monte Carlo.
